name: cook replicate
description: A recipe whose output stays out of commits leaves every new clone or worktree with the committed `cook.lock` entry but none of the files. `io.github.lmarqs.cookbook:ralph#ralph-tui --share=clone` is the case in point: `.gitignore` keeps all of `.ralph-tui/` out of commits, and its help says "each clone cooks its own". Today the person retypes the original command with all of its arguments, because `cook.lock` records no arguments (ADR 0007, decision 3).  This feature makes `cook.lock` record each recipe's arguments and adds `./cook replicate <recipe>...`. The command cooks each named recipe again, at the source and with the arguments `cook.lock` recorded, through the normal diff, approval and `--dry-run` flow. `discard` and `replicate` both accept the recipe's lock name, such as `io.github.lmarqs.cookbook:ralph#ralph-tui`, without a version. Tracking issue: #71.

userStories.title: Record each recipe's arguments in `cook.lock`
userStories.description: As a person who cooks a recipe, I want `cook.lock` to record the arguments I gave so that the recipe can be cooked again without my retyping them.
acceptanceCriteria: `RecipeRun.run` (`core/src/main/groovy/thecook/cookbook/RecipeRun.groovy:42-62`) returns the normalized argument list to its caller: the `line` it builds for `cookedWith`, without the recipe name. `cookedWith` output is byte-for-byte unchanged.

`CookLock` (`core/src/main/groovy/thecook/cookbook/CookLock.groovy`) stores a nullable `List<String> arguments` per entry. `null` means "not recorded". The field is read in `parse`, taken by `record(...)`, exposed through an accessor `arguments(name)`, and rendered after `sha256` and before `owns` as a list of JSON-quoted strings.
`render()` writes `arguments: []` for a recipe cooked with no arguments.
`version: 1` is unchanged. A lock whose entries have no `arguments` key still parses, and their `arguments(name)` returns `null`.
`CookbookCook.propose` (`core/src/main/groovy/thecook/cookbook/CookbookCook.groovy:51,65`) passes the arguments into `lock.record`.

A new test in `core/src/test/groovy/thecook/CookbookCookTest.groovy` cooks with the inputs of the test at ~:1237 (`agent: [codex, claude, codex], m: [slow], file: [./b.md, a.md, b.md]`). It asserts the lock records `["--agent=codex", "--agent=claude", "--mode=slow", "--file=a.md", "--file=b.md"]`.
Tests also cover `arguments: []` with none given, and the parsing of an entry without `arguments`.

Existing lock-content assertions in `CookbookCookTest`, `RalphTuiCookTest`, `BeadsTrackerCookTest`, `AgentsWorktreeCookTest` and `GitWorktreesCookTest` include the new field. No assertion is loosened.

This repository's `cook.lock` is regenerated by re-cooking its recipes with their current arguments (taken from the `cookedWith` lines in `.gitignore` and the other cooked files), never edited by hand. Its diff only adds `arguments` lines.
Commit: `feat(core): cook.lock records the arguments each recipe was cooked with`
`./gradlew check cliBuild jpackageTest` passes
`git diff --check` passes

userStories.title: Accept the version-less lock name as a recipe operand for discard
userStories.description: As a person discarding a recipe, I want to name it the way `cook.lock` does, such as `io.github.lmarqs.cookbook:ralph#ralph-tui`, so that I don't have to look up its version.
acceptanceCriteria: `RecipeLoader.name` (`core/src/main/groovy/thecook/cookbook/RecipeLoader.groovy:36-40`) maps `group:artifact#recipe` to that same short name. `Coordinates.parse` keeps rejecting it everywhere else. Cooking a version-less coordinate is still refused with the existing message.
`./cook discard io.github.lmarqs.cookbook:agents#connect` removes the same targets as `./cook discard io.github.lmarqs.cookbook:agents:0.0.0#connect`.
Versioned coordinates (any version) and `.groovy` paths still work for discard.
A test in `CookbookCookTest` near the discard refusals (~:1620) discards by lock name. A case in `cli/src/test/groovy/thecook/cli/CookCommandTest.groovy` (~:422) does the same through the CLI.
Commit: `feat(core): discard takes a recipe's name as cook.lock writes it`
`./gradlew check cliBuild jpackageTest` passes
`git diff --check` passes

userStories.title: `CookbookReplicate` in core
userStories.description: As the CLI, I want a core operation that turns lock names into cook requests replaying the recorded source and arguments so that replicate reuses the cook pipeline unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: A new `core/src/main/groovy/thecook/cookbook/CookbookReplicate.groovy`, shaped like `CookbookDiscard.groovy:21-45`, maps each operand to a name through `RecipeLoader.name`.
It refuses an empty operand list, a name given twice, and a name not in `cook.lock`. The last refusal lists the known names, as discard does.
It refuses an entry whose `arguments` is `null` with `<name> has no recorded arguments in cook.lock` and the next step `cook it once with its arguments`.

For each entry it builds `RecipeRequest(entry.source, <arguments parsed back into Argument.inline>)` and returns `new CookbookCook(...).propose(requests)`. The recorded `source`, including its version, decides what loads. A version in the operand is ignored.

When the resolved sha256 differs from the recorded one, the changed-source notice is reported and cooking goes ahead. This covers coordinates (existing notice, `CookbookCook.groovy:61`) and path recipes.

When the recorded arguments no longer bind (`Unknown argument`, a missing required param), the error adds `arguments recorded in cook.lock: <recorded line>` and the next step `cook it with its arguments`.

A new `core/src/test/groovy/thecook/CookbookReplicateTest.groovy` covers: a round trip: cook a recipe with arguments, delete a file it owns, replicate, and get the same files and lock; a second replicate with an empty diff; each refusal above; a path recipe; a drifted source, with the notice shown; recorded arguments the recipe no longer accepts, with the prefixed error.
Commit: `feat(core): replicate cooks a recipe again from its cook.lock entry`
`./gradlew check cliBuild jpackageTest` passes
`git diff --check` passes

userStories.title: `./cook replicate` command word
userStories.description: As a person in a fresh clone, I want `./cook replicate <recipe>...` so that I recreate a recipe's output with one command.
acceptanceCriteria: Before coding, read `docs/features/cli.md`, `docs/features/discard.md` and `docs/ux/cli-standards.md`, as AGENTS.md requires.

`ReplicateArgs` is added to `Grammar` (`cli/src/main/groovy/thecook/cli/terminal/Grammar.groovy:38,85-95`). It takes the `KitchenScoped` mixin (`-C/--kitchen`), `--dry-run` and `--batch-approve` only.

`CookCommand` (`cli/src/main/groovy/thecook/cli/terminal/CookCommand.groovy:139-148,197-215`) dispatches it to a `replicate()` that applies `discard()`'s operand checks and then calls `write(...)` (:368).
An operand starting with `-` is refused with `replicate takes no recipe arguments`, or the existing "goes before the first recipe" text for batch options.
Diagnostics are prefixed `cook: replicate: `.
`./cook --help` lists `replicate` next to `discard` and `help`.
`CookCommandTest` gains a replicate test and error-table rows mirroring discard's (~:422-505). Every `--help` output assertion includes the new usage line.
Commit: `feat(cli): replicate cooks named recipes again with the arguments cook.lock recorded`
`./gradlew check cliBuild jpackageTest` passes
`git diff --check` passes

userStories.title: Decisions and architecture
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the ADRs and the architecture to state that `cook.lock` records arguments and that replicate exists so that no document contradicts the code.
acceptanceCriteria: `docs/adrs/0007-ownership.md` is edited in place, following `docs/adrs/README.md` (present tense, no history): decision 3 lists the recorded arguments; a new reason: a clone that keeps a recipe's output out of commits rebuilds it from the lock; a decision point for replicate sits next to discard (6); decision 7 and reason 7 are restated so they don't contradict replicate: cooking still never skips a recipe, and
`docs/adrs/0030-recipe-connections.md`, `0025-recipes.md`, `0026-cookbook-trust.md` and `0013-organization-content.md` match what the lock holds.

`docs/architecture.md` is updated in: Ownership and the lock (:168-207), including the example YAML; Cooking and discard (:209); Command line (:280-285); FR-14, FR-17 (the command words and the reserved first operand `replicate`) and FR-19.
`grep -rn "records no.*arguments" docs/ cookbook/ core/ README.md` finds nothing.
Commit: `docs(adrs): cook.lock records recipe arguments and replicate replays them`
`./gradlew check cliBuild jpackageTest` passes
`git diff --check` passes

userStories.title: Feature pages, UX standards and recipe help
userStories.description: As a person learning Cook, I want the feature pages and the ralph-tui help to explain replicate so that I find it when a fresh clone lacks a recipe's files.
acceptanceCriteria: A new `docs/features/replicate.md`, modeled on `docs/features/discard.md`, covers: Objective, Overview and Reference; the `--share=clone` worked example; the drift notice; the limit that named recipes cook in the order given, not the original invocation's order.
`docs/features/README.md` links the page from its reading path.

`docs/features/cli.md` is updated in the Synopsis, the Commands table, the reserved first words, the recipe operands (the version-less lock name for discard and replicate) and the batch options table.
`docs/features/discard.md` documents the lock-name operand.
`docs/features/glossary.md` updates the `cook.lock` and Short name entries and adds Replicate.
`docs/ux/cli-standards.md` is updated in Command grammar, Command set and Help text.

`docs/ux/generated-content-standards.md:75-76` and the doc comments in `cookbook/agents/Agents.groovy:129-132,195-198` give the reason the opening line still exists: a reader of the file sees the arguments.

The `cookbook/ralph/ralph-tui.groovy` help (~:276-277) says that a new clone with `--share=clone` runs `./cook replicate io.github.lmarqs.cookbook:ralph#ralph-tui`. Long `@help` lines continue after a trailing `\`.
The root `README.md` "current implementation" list includes replicate.
If any change touches `cookbook/agents/skills/agents-layout/`, `agents#seed` is re-cooked. `.agents/skills/` is never edited by hand.
Commit: `docs(features): replicate and the lock-name operand`
`./gradlew check cliBuild jpackageTest` passes
`git diff --check` passes
